title: fix: reduce PostgreSQL transcript append round trips
body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL sends a separate event insert and identity insert for each ordinary transcript append, adding three database round trips to a normal input, tool-result, and final-answer turn.

## User Impact

Ordinary PostgreSQL appends use fewer round trips inside their existing transactions. Transcript bytes, identity and idempotency behavior, SQLite writes, locks, and final commit authority remain unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The payload inserter can write the event and its identity in one PostgreSQL statement. The identity insert consumes the event's RETURNING rows; the final result reports event acceptance even when an identity conflict is ignored. The existing event-ID guard is preserved for cold scalar appends, while complete resident actors retain their own identity check.

Existing-owner key relocation keeps its ordered path: accept the event, clear the former owner's key, then insert the new identity. Batch/import and strict replacement paths retain their existing writers. The repeated window-touch conditions are carried into the same helper without changing when it writes.

## Evidence

The real actor regression fails on base `03834a76775d` with six event/identity insert trips and passes with three. Its three BEGINs, COMMITs, and advisory locks are unchanged. Exact transcript, identity, active projection, index watermark, search rows/results, replay, rollback, and revoked final commit checks are preserved.

Both-engine semantic tests cover duplicate events and idempotency keys, scan-assistant collisions, successful and rejected ownership relocation, and rollback. A direct PostgreSQL owner test also checks that an ignored identity conflict still reports an accepted event, while an unrelated unique-key conflict rolls the event back.

Final focused proof: **72/72 tests across six files**, including the existing payload, batch, store, and timestamp suites. Infra test execution: 45.48 s; runtime-config execution: 29.47 s; complete wrapper: 155.53 s. The exact PR1 baseline passes all eight original identity cases. Core and infra test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and Kysely guardrails pass. Independent Codex review is clean through P2. Production: +103/−42 lines (net +61); tests: +389; test routing: +1.

Initial CI identified a type-only import cycle; the binding type now derives from the already imported database schema. The exact failed Madge check passes with zero cycles, core typechecking passes, and the type-only repair has a separate clean review.

## Performance

Owner acceptance: the +6.91% full-run p95 is concentrated in the first (cold) turn, a path PR2 does not change, and is within the single-pair Testbox noise band (#178641 moved C=64 throughput 3.49 → 2.57 turns/s with a change that workload never exercises). The deterministic proof is −3 wire trips per warm turn (43.3 → 40.3) with unchanged transactions/locks; throughput +6.42%. A consolidated interleaved A/B/A/B re-measure runs after the pgopt wave.

Frozen local PG17 A/B, three warm turns per arm, with all 63 frozen harness hashes verified:

| Per warm turn | PR1 baseline `03834a76775d` | Candidate `a86affe1e292` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Requests / wire trips / SQL statements | 11.3333 / 43.3333 / 52.3333 | 11.3333 / 40.3333 / 49.3333 |
| BEGIN / COMMIT / advisory locks | 9 / 9 / 9 | 9 / 9 / 9 |
| PostgreSQL errors / rollbacks | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

This removes exactly **three wire trips and three SQL statements per turn**. `acceptInput` uses 8→7 trips; the two append requests use 15→13. Both arms completed all five ordinary turns and restart/readback; the candidate needed one bounded retry of a definite pre-admission startup refusal. Local wall times are not a performance claim. The final head differs from this measured candidate only by the type-only cycle repair above; both production modules emit byte-identical ESM under the pinned esbuild transform.

One Testbox C=64 A/B on the same 8-CPU, 30.95 GiB host, with a fresh PostgreSQL database and Gateway per arm:

| Metric | PR1 baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Completed turns | 320/320 | 320/320 |
| Errors / timeouts | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Throughput, turns/s | 2.424932 | 2.580644 |
| p50 latency, seconds | 26.3135 | 22.7953 |
| p95 latency, seconds | 30.8267 | 32.9565 |
| p99 latency, seconds | 31.7884 | 33.3090 |

Throughput was 6.42% higher, while p95 was 6.91% worse. This is one paired observation, not proof of a general wall-time improvement or a causal tail regression. Both arms completed ordinary turns and restart/readback, each with one bounded pre-admission startup retry. All 320 tool requests and results in each arm completed successfully. Both PostgreSQL containers were removed and their ports verified closed.

Descriptive per-turn p95 for the five-turn workload, using the frozen harness nearest-rank method, in seconds: baseline 30.932 / 30.635 / 31.788 / 28.517 / 26.872; candidate 33.309 / 28.321 / 26.228 / 23.588 / 22.470. The higher full-run tail is concentrated in the first turn across the 64 sessions; all four later-turn p95 observations are lower. This post-run breakdown does not establish the cause or replace the full-run result above.

All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on final head `3927c33fbcca` in [CI run 39482709194](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39482709194). The complete final-head CI run passed.

The rewrite+append prior-event SELECT/conditional UPDATE and extra window touch are outside this change; they require a resident-payload invalidation contract.
